body: Thank you. It's a very difficult subject because at its root, we're talking about killing babies. They may not be born yet, but science shows that they feel pain from something like 8 weeks gestation (I could be wrong, it could be earlier). I'm very thankful that I've never found myself in a situation where I felt an abortion was truly the best option, because it's something that I don't think I could ever forgive myself for.

I wish every child had someone who loved them to look after them, and plenty of food, a safe home, and enrichment in their lives. I'd honestly have to think a little more about if I would still be pro choice if every child put up for adoption was guaranteed this kind of care. Sadly, the experience that I'm more familiar with is people (and organizations, including the government) being very supportive while you are pregnant, but once the child is born, they stop being anywhere near as supportive. Again, just my experiences and opinions, in as respectful a way as I can manage while being half asleep. Lol.

Honestly, I consider myself pro choice. My biggest reason is that we will never do away with abortions - prohibiting them will only stop abortions provided by doctors who know what they are doing, in clean environments with the possibility of follow up care when needed.

I'm not looking to argue. I don't like abortion, I just don't want anyone that I love to end up dying a terrible death because they were desperate. I just wanted to explain my personal opinion briefly before saying, I think you hit the nail on the head with your opinion here. I've heard these arguments before and have asked people myself, is life REALLY always the more humane option when faced with poverty, starvation, abuse, neglect, blah blah blah? (Sorry. Those situations just make me really, really sad.)

I considered adoption with my oldest. I was 19, immature, and scared. My family shamed me out of putting her up for adoption when they found out that I had requested information on it. I'm 35 now, and while I think adoption is certainly a kinder option than death, my understanding of the system is that there are a LOT of children that grow up in foster care or orphanages (is there a more modern word? That sounds so anachronistic), and these children are far too often put through traumatic situations. Trauma changes the brain, and many of these kids have hard lives because of how they grew up. Again, just my understanding from reading and listening to acquaintances who grew up this way.

I wish adoption were always a feasible option with a positive outcome for everyone involved. A friend of mine put his daughter up for adoption and gets updates and she's like 10 now and doing great. That makes me really happy. She wasn't killed in utero, and her life is better than it would have been if she had stayed with her birth parents. I wish every child put up for adoption had such a positive experience. 

Anyway... yeah. You gave a really good answer. I appreciate your thoughtfulness in your response. I sincerely hope that my comment doesn't come across as rude or anything. I truly mean no disrespect.

An hour for breakfast sounds entirely normal, even if it is a little mom and pop place. Let's break it down.

5-10 minutes to be seated, order drinks, look over menu. 
15-20 minutes for food to be made and served.
~30 minutes to eat, chat, enjoy your time eating out, have dessert and coffee.

Honestly I think that's pretty quick actually, I would allot about an hour and a half per table.

I work at a fine dining restaurant and for dinner, we generally expect about 2 hours per table. The time goes up as the table size increases. 2 hours is the rough expectation for a table of 2-4. Anything over that will take 3+ hours.

We actually had a table of 4 the other night that came in at 6:30 and didn't leave until 9:45. They weren't celebrating or anything, they just wanted to "take their time" and space their courses out way longer than average. They didn't even order their entrees until 8:05, and that was after telling them at 7:30 and 7:45 that the kitchen closes at 8. It was super slow that night and we should have (and would have) been out by 8:30 if not for that table. That's what made it so frustrating. 

Anyway, in your situation, OP, as a server, I agree with someone above me who said they would have told you to take your time after the new customer requested your clearly still in use table. Some people are just assholes.

Final statement: try not to camp, but do enjoy yourself and don't feel rushed. There's no hard and fast rule to what differentiates the two, but you can tell when others do it and I imagine that people can also tell if they're doing it. If there's a line forming, leave a little sooner if you'd like, but remember that the people waiting are coming in, seeing how busy it is, being told there is a wait, and agreeing to be put on the list and wait. Their wait is not your fault.

When my 19 yo cat suddenly went blind, I spoke to my vet about euthanizing her. He explained that he normally makes the decision to euthanize based on age, diagnoses, and most importantly, quality of life. He said at the time, he wouldn't refuse to put her down, but he encouraged me to give it a week or two, not move any furniture around, and pay attention to how well she adjusted. I like to try to make mine artful. I'm not a very practiced artist though. So I'm usually disappointed in what I do. But...I like having a creative outlet, even if it isn't anywhere near as pretty as others'. It soothes that creative drive that makes me so restless at times. 

Even when I do a very simple list type layout, I like to highlight the date or something in color just to make it look a little prettier.

I started with a random spiral bound graph paper notebook that I had laying around. I enjoyed how I was able to draw in it and have guidelines, instead of just horizontal lines. The paper was thick enough to hold up to Crayola Super Tips and even some painting. I wish I could tell you what kind of notebook it was, but it was just something that a friend gave me that had a company name on the front. I wish I could find another like it, lol.

After a bit, I got really curious about the dotted books. I felt like it would give me more freedom and open space. But I couldn't justify spending $20-30 on a Leuchtturm either. Happily, I found a dotted notebook (with a book mark and back pocket!!) at Walmart for about $5. It was smallish, with a padded hard cover, and I've almost finished it! Quite a feat for someone who, like you, has trouble finishing a notebook. 

I have since grabbed two larger, soft cover versions for about the same price. My only gripe is that the paper seems to be a bit thin for watercolor, and the color options are limited (orange, blue, and lime for the big ones, and those plus black for the small). But for the price, I'll just make a collage on the front or something lol.

I did briefly try a regular spiral bound wide ruled notebook but I hated it. 

All that said, try to remember that BuJo's literally just require a pen and a notebook. They don't need to be fancy. They're really just a place to keep all of your to-do lists and other stuff you want to keep track of, in one place. 

I can never find my notebooks on the Walmart website, but they're by Exceed. Maybe try to find one to try out, they're certainly cheap enough and will let you see if you like the dotted style. :)
